How to keep your school running when cyber issues strike

When a cyber issue hits, what matters most is not just whether it can be prevented, but how quickly your school can get back to normal. These two ideas – your security posture and your security resilience – work side by side to help protect your school or kura.

Your security posture helps prevent incidents. Your security resilience helps you recover quickly when they occur. 

In this blog, we’ll break down the difference, share two short school-based scenarios, and offer simple checklists to help you strengthen each area.

What ‘security posture’ means

Your security posture is the current state of your school’s cybersecurity readiness. It’s all about how well protected you are right now, and how strong and mature your defences are today. It includes things like:

  • Your existing security controls (such as firewalls or multi-factor authentication)
  • Policies and procedures
  • Technical vulnerabilities and patching levels
  • Risk management processes
  • Staff awareness and training

The National Cyber Security Centre’s critical controls are a great place to start when looking at improving your security posture.

What we mean by ‘security resilience’

Your security resilience is your ability to prepare for, cope with, recover from, and adapt to cybersecurity incidents. It’s less about the state of your defences today and more about what happens when something goes wrong. It includes:

  • Incident response capability
  • Business continuity planning
  • Disaster recovery processes
  • Backups and restoration
  • Learning and improving after an incident

Why schools need both: a tale of two schools

Strong preventative measures (posture) can fall without a good recovery plan (resilience), and vice versa. A complete strategy requires both.How posture and resilience work together

A strong security posture reduces the chance of a cyber incident.

Strong security resilience reduces the impact when something does happen.

Modern cyber strategies recognise that no defence is perfect. Resilience is essential because it keeps teaching and learning going, even on a challenging day.

Final thoughts

Strengthening both your security posture and your security resilience gives your school or kura the best chance of staying safe, staying open, and staying focused on what matters most – supporting your kaiako and ākonga to thrive.

In the same way that learning to drive carefully doesn’t remove the need for car insurance, strong technology and good cyber practices can’t guarantee that nothing will ever go wrong. Some factors will always be outside your control. Security resilience is what helps your school respond calmly, recover quickly, and keep going when the unexpected happens.
